old_description: Since 1978, we've proudly served the Central Oregon community, building lasting relationships and providing the equipment you need to get the job done right. about:
Central Oregon Forklift and Equipment has operated from Bend, Oregon since 1978. The family-owned dealership was founded to serve the Central Oregon community with material handling and outdoor power equipment.

The company stocks new and pre-owned forklifts, tractors, zero-turn mowers, implements, attachments, and shop equipment from brands such as Yale, Bad Boy, LS, and Kioti. It also runs a parts department, offers financing, and provides both mobile and in-shop repair services along with preventative maintenance programs and short-term rentals.

Customers range from construction firms like SunWest Builders to agricultural operators and residential property owners across Central Oregon, including La Pine. The dealership's technicians travel to job sites for same-day repairs and support equipment selection for tasks ranging from land clearing to warehouse material handling.

The owners emphasize straightforward guidance and responsive support, positioning the business as a local partner that treats every customer like family. Mobile service, flexible rental terms, and a focus on minimizing downtime are cited as core reasons customers return.

name: Century Mold
old_description: Century Mold delivers precision-engineered plastic solutions across North America
about:
Century Mold was founded in 1986 in Shelbyville, Tennessee. The company operates as a U.S.-based manufacturer of precision plastic components, with no public disclosure of its ownership structure or founding individuals.

The company provides fully integrated plastic injection molding services, from part and tool design through production and finishing. Its six North American facilities encompass 675,000 square feet and house more than 200 presses ranging up to 2,200 tons of clamping force. A staff of over 50 engineers, designers, and mold builders supports design-for-manufacturability, Moldflow and finite-element analysis, reverse engineering, scanning, and 3D printing. Secondary operations include assembly, multiple welding methods, pad printing, and performance testing.

Century Mold serves automotive, defense, industrial, consumer, lawn-and-garden, and packaging markets. Automotive customers—including OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers such as BorgWarner, Robert Bosch, Delphi, and Visteon—source complex, high-volume components that appear in over 80 percent of vehicles on U.S. roads. Defense programs rely on the company for mission-critical parts produced under secure, fully controlled U.S. manufacturing. Industrial and consumer clients use its in-house engineering and tool-transfer capabilities to bring products to market.

The company emphasizes a localized supply chain and secure, end-to-end production as key differentiators, citing its IATF 16949 and ISO 9001:2015 certifications and a track record of supplier awards from major automotive OEMs. It positions itself as a partner that reduces risk through tool-transfer expertise and disciplined process control.

Century Wire Products Corp. was established in 1998 in Wind Gap, Pennsylvania, drawing on more than 45 years of wire-industry experience. The company is 100% woman-owned; founder Danielle relocated the operation from Washington to Wind Gap in 2009, bringing many employees with her.

The Pennsylvania plant manufactures stainless steel lashing wire, single-end wire, messenger strand, and galvanized EHS Class A strand to ASTM A475 standards, plus galvanized fencing and domestic strand. Primary markets include CATV, telecommunications, and industrial sectors, with products used in broadband and federal infrastructure projects subject to Build America, Buy America requirements. Customers range from contractors to grant recipients; the company supports industry groups such as the Cable Television Engineers Society, the Walter Katz Scholarship Foundation, and the Missouri Cable Technical Association.

Danielle's leadership emphasizes employment of people with disabilities through a long-standing partnership with Abilities of Northwest New Jersey, earning her the Private Enterprise Award from ACCESS NJ. name: Certified Parts Corporation
old_description: Certified Parts Corporation (CPC) was founded in 1982 by James Grafft, with a mission to preserve well known international and local legacy brands that were in danger of extinction.  Initially specializing in manufacturing service parts for these companies, CPC has grown into a major supplier to OEM’s and has brought some of these brands back into production. Comet, TecumsehPower, Wisconsin Wagon and vintage recreational vehicle parts makeup CPC’s current lineup of companies.  CPC owns motorcycles and mini-cycle brands that include Bridgestone and Indian, Rupp, Chaparral and Steen along with a complimentary selection of hard-to-get engine parts that were used in many of the snowmobiles and mini-cycles of the day. A passion for history and recognizing opportunity serves as a guiding principle for Certified Parts Corporation.
about:
Certified Parts Corporation (CPC) was founded in 1982 by James Grafft in Edgerton, Wisconsin. The company began with a mission to preserve well-known international and local legacy brands facing extinction. Grafft’s experience at Fox Corporation in Janesville, where he saw the need for continuous parts supply for defunct manufacturers, led him to purchase the service parts division when Fox shut down in 1976. He later acquired the Bridgestone brand on his 26th birthday and established CPC in 1982, acquiring the Arctic Cat snowmobile division from bankruptcy.

Today, CPC operates a 200,000-square-foot factory in Edgerton where it manufactures original service parts, including carburetors and the full line of Comet torque converters and clutches. The company acquires legacy brands—such as TecumsehPower, Comet, Hoffco, Wisconsin Wagon, and vintage recreational vehicle lines—and restarts production of their components. It also manages extensive parts inventories and provides distribution and service support through a worldwide dealer network.

CPC serves OEMs and aftermarket customers in recreational, construction, agricultural, and marine industries. Its brand portfolio includes snowmobile, mini-cycle, watercraft, and outdoor power equipment lines. Concrete examples include supplying Comet clutches to OEM manufacturers across multiple sectors and supporting engines for snowmobiles, mini-cycles, and utility equipment through the Lauson, Snow King, and LCT brands.

The company’s guiding principle is a passion for history and recognizing opportunity in orphaned brands. By acquiring intellectual property, tooling, and inventory, CPC keeps legacy products running and reintroduces historic names to the market, such as the 1895 Lauson engine line.

name: Champlain Cable Corporation
old_description: Champlain Cable manufactures copper and aluminum wire and tubing. Based in upstate New York, products include building wire, refrigerant tubing and electrical construction materials serving HVAC and construction industries.
about:
Champlain Cable Corporation was founded in 1946 in Plattsburgh, New York. The company began as a manufacturer of copper and aluminum wire and tubing for building and refrigeration applications.

Today, Champlain Cable designs and manufactures high-performance wire and cable solutions using electron beam cross-linking, custom polymer compounds, and advanced insulation systems. The company operates with 50 to 199 employees and maintains in-house irradiation, testing, research and development, and custom engineering capabilities. Its product portfolio includes branded lines such as EXAR, EXRAD, EXRAD Rail, DATACLEAR, and DATARAD, serving applications from automotive and rail to military shipboard communications.

The company serves a broad range of industries including automotive, aerospace, military, industrial, marine, rail, truck and bus, agricultural, mining, construction, HVAC, plumbing, and electrical. Customers include OEMs, Tier 1 suppliers, and government agencies such as the U.S. Navy, for which Champlain Cable developed QPL-accepted DATACLEAR data cables for shipboard use. A distribution partnership with Cameron Connect provides quick-turn access to EXRAD-Rail products for the North American rail transit market.

Champlain Cable emphasizes its leadership in irradiated cross-linked technology and polymer science, combining engineering expertise, field knowledge, and manufacturing excellence to deliver superior durability, flexibility, and thermal resistance in extreme environments. The company was built to solve complex challenges in mission-critical applications where long-term reliability is essential.

name: Champlain Metals
old_description: Champlain Metals offers design and metal fabrication solutions for structural and ornamental metal work. John Marius carries on the old world passion for detail rooted in the traditions learned from working in the New York metropolitan area and the Champagne and Alsatian regions of France.
about:
Champlain Metals was founded in 2004 by John Marius in Burlington, Vermont. Marius, who trained with the French artisans' guild Compagnons du Devoir, brought metalworking traditions from the Champagne and Alsatian regions of France and the New York metropolitan area to the Champlain Valley.

The shop provides design, custom fabrication, casting, and forging for structural and ornamental metalwork. Its output ranges from architectural elements such as stair stringers, bronze cap rails, and awning brackets to finished goods like garden trowels, side tables, and heat exchangers. The facility handles both one-off commissions and production runs, though specific capacity figures are not disclosed.

Clients include contractors, architects, and private customers throughout the Champlain Valley and beyond. Project examples cited on the company's site include stair stringers for a contractor named Andrew Russel, a heat exchanger for a residential client, and forged bronze brackets for architectural installations.

Marius emphasizes an old-world passion for detail rooted in his guild training and European experience, positioning the company as a keeper of traditional metalworking methods while serving modern structural and decorative needs.

about:
Charleston Steel operates from Dunbar, West Virginia, where it has been supplying steel to the construction industry since 1989. The company is led by President John E. Goetz IV and has accumulated over 34 years of fabrication experience.

The shop functions as a full‑service structural steel fabricator and value‑added steel service center. Its core output includes fabricated structural steel, joists and deck, stairs and handrail, simple bridges and bridge components, as well as material‑handling and heavy‑duty weighing equipment. The facility holds AISC certification and AWS Certified Welding Fabricator status, with welding procedures covering all joints, processes and positions.

Customers span commercial and industrial construction, the material‑handling and weighing sectors, and state departments of highways for bridge work. The company’s central West Virginia location provides interstate access to East Coast shipping ports.

Charleston Steel emphasizes a customer‑oriented philosophy built on competitive pricing, on‑time delivery and a quality system audited annually by Quality Management Company, LLC. Its AISC and AWS certifications underscore a commitment to consistent, documented fabrication standards.

about:
Chaucer Foods is headquartered in Forest Grove, Oregon, and traces its origins to a bakery opened in Kent, England. The company does not disclose a founding year or ownership structure, but its history emphasizes a progression from that first bakery to a global ingredient supplier.

The company manufactures freeze-dried and baked ingredients for retail and foodservice brands worldwide. It operates manufacturing and development facilities in the United States, the United Kingdom, Europe, and China, leveraging proprietary software to track its supply chain and employing agronomists who work directly with farmers. Chaucer offers custom ingredient formulation, application development for beverages, confectionery, bakery, and foodservice, and compliance with third-party audits.

Chaucer serves major retail and foodservice brands across the food and beverage industry. Its ingredients are used in beverage, confectionery, bakery, and foodservice applications, and the company says it immerses itself in market trends to deliver localized executions for diverse industries.

Chaucer says its differentiation lies in a customer-focused partnership model, with research and applications teams that bring creative and technical solutions. The company highlights its global manufacturing footprint, world-technologies for customization, and a commitment to sustainable, ethically sourced, clean-label ingredients as the drivers of its success.
